title: Winchell, the theme song and the 1933 Europe trip
summary: Asked for the year, Thomas says 1929-31 and Walter Winchell kept requesting the tune.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Do you remember what year that was, Foots, approximately?
It had to be 29, 30 or 31; those were the early years of the band.
So did you get to make the trip to Europe in '33?
Yeah, I made it to Europe. The band had gained quite a bit by that time. So...
Tell us about that. What was that band like?

Well, the band was a good band. But one thing, we were popular... And let me tell you the instance how I had to change...I changed from... Well, one thing I'll tell you, what made "Minnie The Moocher" popular. The writer, the biggest writer... We had already played "Minnie The Moocher;" we had to play it again for him.
No, the newspaper writer. The biggest one,...

Walter Winchell. Every time he'd come in the club, if we'd already played it, we had to play it again for him. He liked it. And we used it as our theme song. I don't know how we happened to start using our theme song. Maybe Mills suggested it. But it was a good thing to do as our theme song.
